page: Microsoft Azure NC48ads_A100_v4 is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine from the NCADSA100v4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 48 dedicated physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 7V13 processor operating at 3.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The server is equipped with 440.0 GB of system memory, providing 9.17 GB per core. Acceleration is delivered via two NVIDIA A100 Ampere GPUs with a combined 160 GB of VRAM. Local storage consists of a 2051 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance supports Premium Storage.

Benchmark results show top-tier performance in LLM inference tasks. Prompt processing speeds reach 8361.48 tokens/sec for a 135M model, 3522.73 tokens/sec for a 7B model, and 501.25 tokens/sec for a 70B model. Text generation speeds are also in the top tier for 7B and 70B models, at 141.58 and 23.97 tokens/sec respectively. Geekbench image processing and Passmark memory scores also rank in the top 10%. Strong top-25% performance is observed in multi-core CPU execution, software compilation, ray tracing, and Redis SET operations, which reach 75.26 million operations per second.

While the server exhibits exceptional memory and GPU capabilities, large-block memory bandwidth (155.26 GB/sec read, 73.43 GB/sec write) and single-threaded text processing fall into the average tier. The qualitative cost profile reflects a high-density resource allocation where the integration of dual A100 GPUs and substantial local NVMe storage offsets the premium hardware class, making it highly efficient for specialized parallel computing rather than basic sequential processing.

This configuration is suited for large language model inference, deep learning training, image processing, ray tracing, and database operations requiring high-speed local storage and substantial memory capacity.
